risk beta means that for every one unit of risk added, the log(odds of selecting a treatment) increase by beta

```{r prepare data, echo=FALSE}
options(scipen=999)

load("~/Dropbox/Medaglia_RiskBenefit_Neuroethics/Pilot_Data/Study1_Project/RiskBenefit_Neuroethics/data/Cleaned_Pilot/clean_task_data.2020.27.12.RData")
load("~/Dropbox/Medaglia_RiskBenefit_Neuroethics/DATA_ANALYSIS/marginal.effect.RData")

Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
dplyr::select(user_id,risk,gain,condition, experimental_treatment_selected, Yes, No,
              age, sex, Income, education, race_ethnicity, Optimize,GRiPs_Score,
               republican, democrat, independent, conservative, liberal, Political_Party, Harm, Fairness,Loyalty,Athority, Sancticy) %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>% #group by user id
  mutate(risk.c = scale(risk, scale = F)) %>% #mean center variables
  mutate(gain.c = scale(gain, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0))  -> logit.data 

m.logit <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) glm(treatment ~ risk.c*gain.c, data = x, family = binomial(link = "logit")))

#m.gam <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) 
 # gam(treatment ~ s(risk) + s(gain), 
  #    data = x, 
   #   family = binomial(link = "logit")))

m.poly <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) 
  glm(treatment ~ poly(risk.c, 2) + poly(gain.c, 2) + risk.c:gain.c, 
      data = x, 
      family = binomial(link = "logit")))


#here is the code that I use to get the subjects
##extract subject betas 
n = nrow(logit.data)/75
user_id <- names(m.logit)
betas <- list()
colin <- list()

for (i in 1:n){
dat = m.logit[[i]]$coefficients
  betas[[i]] = dat
}
subjectModels <- do.call(rbind, betas)
colnames(subjectModels) <-  c('Intercept', 'Risk_Beta', 'Gain_Beta', 'Interaction')
subjectModels <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels)

#check the variance inflation factors 
for (i in user_id){
vif <- car::vif(m.logit[[i]])
colin[[i]] <- vif
}

subjectcolin <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, colin))
subjectcolin <- tibble::rownames_to_column(subjectcolin, "user_id")

#remove subject if they have vif for risk or gain above 4 
subjectcolin %>% 
  filter(!risk.c > 4) %>% 
  filter(!gain.c > 4) -> index 


#merge the subject models extracted above and the index
subjectModels <- merge(subjectModels, index, "user_id")


#create data that only contains subjects after VIF data exculsion
data <- merge(logit.data, subjectModels, "user_id")
data %>% 
   mutate(conservatismFactor = republican + conservative - democrat - liberal) %>% 
   #mutate(inverse.risk = -Risk_Beta) %>% 
   mutate(lambda = -Risk_Beta/Gain_Beta) %>%
   mutate(Risk_odds = exp(Risk_Beta)) %>%
   mutate(Gain_odds = exp(Gain_Beta)) %>%
   mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.80 | No >= 75 *.80, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
   mutate(loss_aversion = as.factor(ifelse(lambda > 1, "loss_aversion", "Not_loss_aversion"))) %>% 
   mutate(risk_aversion = as.factor(ifelse(Risk_odds > 1, "risk_seeking", "risk_aversion"))) %>% 
   dplyr::select(c("user_id","condition", "age", "Income", "education", "Risk_Beta", "Gain_Beta", "conservatismFactor", "Political_Party", "Harm", "Fairness", "Loyalty", "Athority", "Sancticy", "GRiPs_Score", "lambda", "loss_aversion", "risk_aversion", "Risk_odds","Gain_odds","Yes", "No","dominate")) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(CogMotor = as.factor(ifelse(condition == "Motor Function", "Motor", "Cognitive"))) -> data 

#colnames(subjectModels) <-  c('user_id', 'marginal.risk', 'marginal.gain' 'marginal.Interaction')
data <- merge(data, XXX, "user_id")

#save(data, file = paste("../DATA_ANALYSIS/clean_task_data.2020.09.14.RData"))

shapiro.test(data$risk5)
shapiro.test(data$gain5)

#t.test(Gain_Beta ~ dominate, data = data)
#t.test(Risk_Beta ~ dominate, data = data)

#data %>% 
#  filter(!dominate == "dominate") -> data


data$guaussian.risk <- LambertW::Gaussianize(data$Risk_Beta)
data$guaussian.gain <- LambertW::Gaussianize(data$Gain_Beta)

#shapiro.test(data$guaussian.risk)
#shapiro.test(data$guaussian.gain)

data$Agecat   <-cut(data$age, c(18,24,49,75))
data$Incomecat<-cut(data$Income, c(0, 25000,50000,75000, 200000))
```
We then added participants’ ratings of themselves as ‘‘Conservative’’
‘‘Republican’’ and subtracted their ratings for ‘‘Liberal’’ and ‘‘Democrat’’ to form a composite measure of conservatism, where higher numbersindicate more conservatism.  where higher numbers indicate more conservatism


```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
 dplyr::select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected, GRiPs_Score, age, Optimize, sex, education) %>% 
  mutate(risk.c = scale(risk, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(gain.c = scale(gain, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(conditionSUM = C(condition, sum)) -> test

  #filter(!user_id == "tTZWd9tg") %>% 
  #filter(!user_id == "ZJ8tICU0") %>% 
  #filter(!user_id == "FIvIqXVg") %>% 
  #filter(!user_id == "4lsMLrPn") %>% 
  #filter(!user_id == "NEFYx2OX")-> test

mlm <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk.c + gain.c + GRiPs_Score + conditionSUM + (risk.c + gain.c | user_id),  
                    data = test, family = binomial, 
                    control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
                    nAGQ = 0) 

mlm.1 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk.c + gain.c + GRiPs_Score + conditionSUM + GRiPs_Score*risk.c + (risk.c + gain.c | user_id),  
                    data = test, family = binomial, 
                    control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
                    nAGQ = 0) 

mlm.2 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk.c + gain.c + GRiPs_Score + conditionSUM + GRiPs_Score*risk.c +GRiPs_Score*gain.c+ (risk.c + gain.c | user_id),  
                    data = test, family = binomial, 
                    control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
                    nAGQ = 0) 
summary(mlm.1)

anova(mlm,mlm.1)

Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
 dplyr::select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected)
ggplot(Neuroethics_Judgement[1:3000,],aes(risk, fill =experimental_treatment_selected)) + geom_density(alpha = .8) +theme(legend.position="none")  +
  facet_wrap(~ user_id, scale = "free_y", nrow = 4, ncol = 10) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 35, linetype="dashed", size=1.5)
```

```{r}
data$Agecat   <-cut(data$age, c(18,24,49,75))
data$Incomecat<-cut(data$Income, c(0, 25000,50000,75000, 200000), right = F)
#calculate Religion
data %>% 
   dplyr::select(ReligionRaised, ReligionNow, Religiosity, Spirituality, 
AttendChurch, ReligiousActivity) %>% 
  mutate(ReligionChanged = data$ReligionRaised == data$ReligionNow) -> religious
religious$ReligionChanged <- factor(religious$ReligionChanged, labels = c("Yes","No")) 
data$ReligionChanged <- factor(religious$ReligionChanged, labels = c("Yes","No")) 

religious <- data.matrix(religious[,c(3:7)]) - 1
religious.efa <- fa(religious, nfactors = 1, rotate = "oblimin", fm ="ml", cor = "poly", scores = "regression")
print(religious.efa$loadings, cutoff = "0.3")
data$ReligiousFactor<- religious.efa$scores
```

```{r univariate and multi regression}
data %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, Risk_Beta, Gain_Beta, age, Agecat, Income, Incomecat, education, sex, conservatismFactor, GRiPs_Score, ReligiousFactor, ReligionNow, Religiosity, inverse.risk)  -> test

lm.1 <- lm(inverse.risk ~age, test)
lm.2 <- lm(inverse.risk ~Income, test)
lm.3 <- lm(inverse.risk ~education, test) #needs recode
lm.4 <- lm(inverse.risk ~sex, test)
lm.5 <- lm(inverse.risk ~conservatismFactor, test)
lm.6 <- lm(inverse.risk ~GRiPs_Score, test)
lm.7 <- lm(inverse.risk ~ReligiousFactor, test)
lm.8 <- lm(inverse.risk ~Religiosity, test)

lm.1 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~Agecat + Gain_Beta, test)
lm.2 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~Incomecat+ Gain_Beta, test)
lm.3 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~education + Gain_Beta, test) #needs recode
lm.4 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~sex + Gain_Beta, test)
lm.5 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~conservatismFactor + Gain_Beta, test)
lm.6 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~GRiPs_Score + Gain_Beta, test)
lm.7 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~ReligiousFactor + Gain_Beta, test)
lm.8 <- lm(Risk_Beta ~Religiosity+ Gain_Beta, test)


lm.multi <- lm(Risk_Beta ~ Gain_Beta + age + Income+ education + sex + conservatismFactor + GRiPs_Score + ReligiousFactor, test)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.1,lm.2,lm.3,lm.4, lm.5, lm.6,lm.7,lm.8, lm.multi), tidy)
#%>% filter(!term == "(Intercept)")
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")])

ggplot(data=test, aes(x=age, y=inverse.risk)) +

ggplot(data=test, aes(x=Income, y=inverse.risk)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +
    geom_point()

ggplot(data=test, aes(x=conservatismFactor, y=inverse.risk)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +
        geom_point()


ggplot(data=test, aes(x=ReligiousFactor, y=inverse.risk)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +
    geom_point()

ggplot(data=test, aes(x=GRiPs_Score, y=inverse.risk)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +

ggplot(test, aes(Agecat, inverse.risk, fill = Agecat)) + geom_boxplot()
ggplot(test, aes(Incomecat, inverse.risk, fill = Incomecat)) + geom_boxplot()






cooks.distance(lm.multi)

cooksd <- cooks.distance(lm.multi)


plot(cooksd, pch="*", cex=2, main="Influential Obs by Cooks distance")  # plot cook's distance
abline(h = 4*mean(cooksd, na.rm=T), col="red")  # add cutoff line
text(x=1:length(cooksd)+1, y=cooksd, labels=ifelse(cooksd>4*mean(cooksd, na.rm=T),names(cooksd),""), col="red")  # add labels

influential <- as.numeric(names(cooksd)[(cooksd > 4*mean(cooksd, na.rm=T))])  # influential row numbers
head(test[influential, ])  # influential observations.

car::outlierTest(lm.multi)


# calculate means, standard deviations,
# standard errors, and 95% confidence 
# intervals by rank
plotdata <- data %>%
   filter(!user_id == "8J7DEjTW") %>%
   filter(!user_id == "RsCXBTrX") %>%
   filter(!user_id == "AC9GykMn") %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "PLOGdhfT") %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "PRK1trPJ") %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "js8aH9h5")%>% 
  group_by(Political_Party) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(lambda),
         sd = sd(lambda),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))
ggplot(plotdata, 
       aes(x = Political_Party, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1)

# calculate means and standard errors by age and sex
plotdata <- data %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "8J7DEjTW") %>%
   filter(!user_id == "RsCXBTrX") %>%
   filter(!user_id == "AC9GykMn") %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "PLOGdhfT") %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "PRK1trPJ") %>% 
   filter(!user_id == "js8aH9h5")%>% 
  group_by(Agecat, sex) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean = mean(lambda),
            sd = sd(lambda),
            se = sd/sqrt(n))

# plot the means and standard errors by sex
ggplot(plotdata, aes(x = Agecat,
                     y = mean, 
                     group=sex, 
                     color=sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin  =mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean+se), 
                width = .1)
```

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Definition of a `keep` function that only selects data points that are between 
# +/- 3 standard deviations of a variable
keep <- function(x) {
(x >= mean(x) - 3*sd(x)) & 
(x <= mean(x) + 3*sd(x))  
}
# Selecting these data points with `filter` and assigning them to a new data set
data_clean <- data %>% 
  filter(keep(school1) &
           keep(school2) &
           keep(school3) &
           keep(self1) &
           keep(self2) &
           keep(friends1) &
           keep(friends2) &
           keep(fam1) &
           keep(fam2) &
           keep(fam3))
```


Winsorization began as a way to "robustify" the sample mean, which is sensitive to extreme values. To obtain the Winsorized mean, you sort the data and replace the smallest k values by the (k+1)st smallest value. You do the same for the largest values, replacing the k largest values with the (k+1)st largest value. The mean of this new set of numbers is called the Winsorized mean. If the data are from a symmetric population, the Winsorized mean is a robust unbiased estimate of the population mean.
```{r trying outlier removal, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(DescTools)
data$outRisk <- DescTools::Winsorize(data$Risk_Beta)
data$outGain <- DescTools::Winsorize(data$Gain_Beta)

dataLong <-
  distinct(dplyr::select(morals, user_id, outRisk, outGain)) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = "user_id", variable.name = "type", value.name = "Beta") 
ggplot(dataLong, aes(x=type, y=Beta, fill=type)) + geom_boxplot()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_boot, geom = "errorbar", color = "red") + 
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "red")

#one way t-test for risk to that of zero
t1 <- t.test(morals$outRisk, mu=0, var.equal=TRUE)
#one way t-test for gain to that of zero
t2 <- t.test(morals$outGain, mu=0, var.equal=TRUE)

morals[, 70:71] <- apply(morals[,70:71], 2, function(X) abs(X))

#two way t-test for risk and gain
t3 <- t.test(morals$outRisk, morals$outGain, paired=TRUE)


#dat <- data.h.long[order(data.h.long$type, data.h.long$user_id), ]
#morals[, 3:4] <- apply(morals[,3:4], 2, function(X) log1p(X)) #this worked fine

aovrisk <- aov(outRisk ~ condition, data=morals)
aovgain <- aov(outGain ~ condition, data=morals)

summary(aovrisk)
summary(aovgain)
# Tukey test to study each of the conditions:
TUKEYrisk <- TukeyHSD(aovrisk)
TUKEYgain <- TukeyHSD(aovgain)
#test representation :
par(mar=c(5,20,4,1)+.1)
plot(TUKEYrisk , las=1 , col="orange")
knitr::kable(TUKEYrisk$condition)

par(mar=c(5,20,4,1)+.1)
plot(TUKEYgain , las=1 , col="blue")
knitr::kable(TUKEYgain$condition)
# Paired t-test
#t3 <- t.test(beta ~ type, dat, paired=TRUE)
library(broom)
library(purrr)
#create table
tab <- map_df(list(t1, t2, t3), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("method","estimate", "statistic", "conf.low", "conf.high", "p.value")])
```

```{r}
options(scipen=999)

load("../data/Cleaned_Pilot/clean_task_data.2020.27.12.RData") 

Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
dplyr::select(user_id,risk,gain,condition, experimental_treatment_selected, Yes, No,
              age, sex, Income, education, race_ethnicity, Optimize,
               republican, democrat, independent, conservative, liberal, Political_Party) %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>% 
  mutate(risk.c = scale(risk, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(gain.c = scale(gain, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) -> logit.data

m.logit <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) glm(treatment ~ risk.c*gain.c, data = x, family = binomial(link = "logit"),control=glm.control(maxit=50)))

#m.logit <- by(logit.data, logit.data$user_id, function(x) glm(treatment ~ poly(risk.c, 3) + poly(gain.c,3), data = x, family = binomial(link = "logit"),control=glm.control(maxit=50)))

n = nrow(logit.data)/75
user_id <- names(m.logit)
datalist.2 <- list()
colin <- list()

for (i in 1:n){
dat = m.logit[[i]]$coefficients
  datalist.2[[i]] = dat
}
subjectModels <- do.call(rbind, datalist.2)
colnames(subjectModels) <-  c('Intercept', 'Risk_Beta', 'Gain_Beta', 'Interaction')
subjectModels <- cbind.data.frame(user_id, subjectModels)
data <- merge(logit.data, subjectModels, "user_id")

data %>% 
   mutate(conservatismFactor = republican + conservative - democrat - liberal) -> data 
   #mutate(inverse.risk = -Risk_Beta) -> data 
predicted.data <- list()
for (i in user_id){
  sub = filter(data, user_id == i)
dat = data.frame(user_id = sub$user_id,
             condition = sub$condition,
            # Risk_Beta = sub$Risk_Beta,
            # Gain_Beta = sub$Gain_Beta,
             treatment = sub$treatment,
             probability.of.treatment=m.logit[[i]][["fitted.values"]],
             Yes = sub$Yes,
             No = sub$No,
             risk = sub$risk,
             gain = sub$gain,
             sex = sub$sex,
             age =  sub$age,
             education = sub$education, 
             conservatismFactor = sub$conservatismFactor,
             Political_Party = sub$Political_Party,
             Optimize = sub$Optimize
             )
predicted.data[[i]] <- dat
}
test <- do.call(rbind, predicted.data)

for (i in user_id){
vif <- car::vif(m.logit[[i]]) 
colin[[i]] <- vif
}

subjectcolin <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, colin))
subjectcolin <- tibble::rownames_to_column(subjectcolin, "user_id")
subjectcolin %>% 
  filter(!risk.c > 4) %>% 
  filter(!gain.c > 4)  -> index 
data <- merge(test, index, "user_id")


test %>% 
 # filter(!probability.of.treatment == 1) %>% 
#  filter(!Yes < 25) %>% 
 # filter(!No < 25) %>% 
   dplyr::select(user_id, condition,  risk, gain, probability.of.treatment) %>% 
   melt(id = c("user_id","condition","probability.of.treatment"), variable.name = "treatment", value.name = "amount") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=amount, y=probability.of.treatment, group = treatment, color = treatment)) +
  xlab("Amount") +
  ylab("Predicted probability choosing an experimental treatment") +
  stat_smooth(method="glm", se=TRUE, fullrange=TRUE, 
              method.args = list(family=quasibinomial))+
  scale_x_continuous("Amount", breaks=seq(5,90,5), limits=c(5,90))+
  scale_y_continuous("Predicted probability choosing an experimental treatment", breaks=seq(0,1,.25), limits=c(0, 1))+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype="dashed", size=1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5,linetype="dashed", size=1) +
  theme_minimal()
  #theme(legend.position="none")
  #facet_wrap(~ condition, scale = "free_y", nrow = 4)

data %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, inverse.risk, Gain_Beta) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  melt(id = c("user_id"), variable.name = "type", value.name = "beta") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(beta, fill=type)) + geom_density(alpha = .8) +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position="none") +
  facet_wrap(~ type, scale = "free_y", nrow = 2) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dashed", size=1.5)

data %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, condition, Risk_Beta, Gain_Beta, inverse.risk, age, Income, education, conservatismFactor) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(CogMotor = ifelse(condition == "Motor Function", "Motor", "Cognitive")) -> data


data$guaussian.risk <- LambertW::Gaussianize(data$Risk_Beta)
data$guaussian.gain <- LambertW::Gaussianize(data$Gain_Beta)
data$Agecat   <-cut(data$age, c(18,24,49,75))
data$Incomecat<-cut(data$Income, c(0, 25000,50000,75000, 200000))

t1 <- t.test(data$guaussian.risk, mu=0, var.equal=TRUE)
#one way t-test for gain to that of zero
t2 <- t.test(data$guaussian.gain, mu=0, var.equal=TRUE)


#two way t-test for risk and gain
data %>% 
  mutate(abs.risk = abs(Risk_Beta)) %>% 
  mutate(abs.gain = abs(Gain_Beta)) -> test
t3 <- t.test(test$abs.risk, test$abs.gain, paired=TRUE)

#create table
tab <- map_df(list(t1, t2, t3), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("method","estimate", "statistic", "conf.low", "conf.high", "p.value")], caption = "Raw data test")


t.test(guaussian.risk ~ CogMotor, test)
t.test(guaussian.gain ~ CogMotor, test)


ggplot(test, 
       aes(x = Risk_Beta, 
           fill = condition)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Risk distribution by Condition")

ggplot(test, 
       aes(x = Risk_Beta, 
           fill = CogMotor)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Risk distribution by Cog-Motor")

ggplot(test, 
       aes(x = Gain_Beta, 
           fill = condition)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Gain distribution by Condition")

ggplot(test, 
       aes(x = Gain_Beta, 
           fill = CogMotor)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Gain distribution by Cog-Motor")

data %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, condition, guaussian.risk, guaussian.gain, Agecat, Incomecat, education, conservatismFactor) %>% 
  mutate(education_recode = fct_recode(education,
  HighSchool = "less than high school",
  HighSchool = "high school degree",
  Undergraduate = "bachelor",
  Postgraduate = "masters",
  Postgraduate = "Doctoral/Professional"
)) %>% 
  mutate(age_recode = fct_recode(Agecat,
  "18-24" = "(18,24]",
  "25-49" = "(24,49]",
  "50-75" = "(49,75]"
)) %>% 
  mutate(income_recode = fct_recode(Incomecat,

  "> 75,000" = "(7.5e+04,2e+05]"
)) %>% 
  mutate(educationSUM = C(education_recode, sum)) %>%

#%>% filter(!term == "(Intercept)")

lm.1 <- lm(guaussian.gain ~ageSUM, test)

#build the anova versions
aov.1 <- stats::oneway.test(guaussian.risk ~ age_recode, data = test, var.equal= T)
aov.2 <- stats::oneway.test(guaussian.risk ~ income_recode, data = test, var.equal= T)
aov.3 <- stats::oneway.test(guaussian.risk ~ education_recode, data = test, var.equal= T)

aov.4 <- stats::oneway.test(guaussian.gain ~ age_recode, data = test, var.equal= T)
aov.5 <- stats::oneway.test(guaussian.gain ~ income_recode, data = test, var.equal= T)
aov.6 <- stats::oneway.test(guaussian.gain ~ education_recode, data = test, var.equal= T)

tab <- map_df(list(aov.1,aov.2,aov.3, aov.4,aov.5,aov.6), tidy)

#post hoc test
TukeyHSD(aov(guaussian.gain ~ education_recode, data = test))
```
